property_summary: If the contract has been initialized, calling SetMinSum must revert.
SetMinSum must only revert after initialization has been performed.
SetMinSum writes exactly the input value when not initialized
After calling SetMinSum with any value on an uninitialized contract, the correct version updates MinSum to that value, while the buggy version leaves MinSum at its default of 0.
For any value passed to SetMinSum before initialization, the stored MinSum must equal the passed argument. The bug breaks this by always storing zero regardless of input.
After a call to SetMinSum with any parameter, the returned value of MinSum() in the reference contract must equal the passed _val, while the buggy contract incorrectly returns type(uint).max instead.

After SetLogFile is called by any caller, the LogFile address in the correct contract equals the address passed as argument, while the buggy contract ignores the argument and sets LogFile to zero, breaking the rule for any non-zero input.

After calling Initialized and then SetLogFile with any address, the correct contract stores the given address in LogFile, while the buggy contract always stores zero, so calling SetLogFile with a non-zero address makes the stored LogFile differ.

For any caller that has not yet called Initialized, after calling SetLogFile with an arbitrary address, the LogFile address stored in the contract must equal the sum of the argument and zero, while the buggy version stores zero address, violating the equality for non-zero arguments.

After the contract is fully initialized (Initialized called then SetLogFile called by anyone), the correct contract's LogFile address equals the argument passed to SetLogFile; the buggy contract stores address(0) regardless, so for any non-zero argument the stored address differs.

After the contract is fully initialized, successfully calling Collect triggers a log message via LogFile.AddMessage; the correct contract's LogFile is the address passed to SetLogFile and can be observed by the call succeeding, whereas the buggy contract sets LogFile to address(0), causing the Collect call to revert for any non-empty message log attempt.
Put should not revert for a valid call with zero lock time and no transfer.
A deposit of 0 ether must succeed.

After any sequence of calls to Put, the sum of all Acc balances plus MinSum plus the contract's own ETH balance must never be less than the total ETH that was ever deposited via Put; the bug decreases Acc balances on Put instead of increasing them, causing this invariant to be violated when a Put is made.
After any call to Put, the caller's Acc balance must have increased by msg.value; the bug decreases it, violating this invariant.

After a Put call, the contract's ETH balance (address(c).balance) equals the sum of all Acc balances plus any ETH sent that is locked or unaccounted, which the bug violates by decreasing Acc balance while ETH balance still increases.

After any call to Put, the caller's internal balance (Acc[caller].balance) plus the contract's own ETH balance (address(c).balance) must be at least the initial sum before the call increased by msg.value (i.e., the system-accounted funds integrity is preserved); the bug subtracts msg.value from the caller's balance while the contract still receives the ETH, breaking this invariant.

After a Put call, the caller's Acc balance must be usable as ETH if collected immediately (i.e., any decrease in Acc balance after Collect results in an equivalent ETH transfer to the caller); the bug causes Collect to underflow or revert after a Put+Collect sequence.

After a successful call to Put, the Acc balance of the sender must equal the total Ether received via Put; the bug fails to increase the balance, causing a mismatch between deposited Ether and recorded balance.

After a successful Put call, the sum of all Acc[addr].balance over all addresses exactly equals address(c).balance (the contract's total Ether). The bug fails to increase Acc[msg.sender].balance on Put, so Acc[msg.sender].balance lags behind the Ether actually received, breaking the invariant.

After any sequence of calls to Put, the sum of all Acc[addr].balance over every addr that ever called Put equals the total Ether received by the contract through those calls; the buggy version omits the balance update, so the recorded sum falls short of the contract's actual Ether balance.

After any sequence of calls, the sum of recorded Acc balance and MinSum (if set) for any single address can never exceed the contract's ETH balance plus the sum of all withdrawals; the buggy Put never credits Acc balance, so a deposit without a subsequent collect makes the recorded balance zero while ETH is present, violating this invariant.

After a Put call, the sender's Acc balance must equal the total Ether they have deposited via Put (tracked by summing msg.value from logs); the buggy version omits the balance update, so the contract's recorded balance is zero while the log-sum is non-zero, breaking the equality.
Collect does not revert when called by a sender whose unlock time has not passed.
Collect does not revert when called.
Collect never reverts when called.
Collect does not revert when called with _am > 0 and the contract has sufficient balance.
Collect does not revert when called by a sender with sufficient balance.

The reference contract allows Collect to succeed only when the current block.timestamp exceeds the account's unlockTime, while the buggy version ignores unlockTime and allows Collect to succeed whenever the balance is sufficient, violating the time-lock invariant.
After a user puts funds with a future unlock time, Collect should revert before that time even if the user has sufficient balance, but the bug allows premature withdrawal.

For any user with sufficient balance and MinSum, a Collect call must revert if the block.timestamp is not greater than the user's unlockTime; the buggy version allows the call to succeed, breaking this time-lock invariant.

For any account, a successful Collect call must imply that block.timestamp > the account's unlockTime at the moment of the call; the mutant allows Collect to succeed when block.timestamp <= unlockTime, violating the time-lock invariant.
For any call to Collect that succeeds on the reference contract, the call must also succeed on the buggy contract; the mutant allows more successful withdrawals, violating this inclusion.
A successful Collect call must never increase the contract's ETH balance.
A successful Collect must not increase the caller's Acc balance.
